[USER] User expressed interest in the use of dissonance in Berg's Wozzeck.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The use of dissonance in Berg's Wozzeck reflects the psychological state of the main character, Wozzeck, who is mentally unstable and struggles with conflicting emotions and impulses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Dissonant music expresses Wozzeck's confusion, anxiety, and inner turmoil, conveying his fragile state of mind and descent into madness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Dissonance reflects the social and political upheaval of the time (1914-1922) when Europe was dealing with the aftermath of World War I and the collapse of traditional social structures.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Berg's dissonant music expresses the shock and despair felt by many in the wake of the war.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Dissonance creates a sense of alienation and unease in the audience, challenging their preconceptions of "beautiful" or "pleasing" music.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Dissonant harmonies and jarring rhythms create discomfort and tension, reflecting the chaos depicted in the opera.
